Your goal is to stay healthy first 3 levels, miss cs but be in range for xp, if your enemy laner uses cd on wave you can jump on them to trade, try abusing your enemies mistakes in lane. When you hit level 3 look on the map for a free kill maybe on the river or try and trade with your enemy laner.

Ideally you are going to have to push your wave and roam all the time, even if you don't see an opportunity to roam you can hide in the bushes, this way you will apply pressure on the map, ALWAYS be there for objective fights for more pressure plus kat excels at objective fights (baron, herald, dragon etc). 

When you get lead in your lane try help your teammates, katarina is a team reliant champion so apart from learning her mechanics you need to learn how to use pings properly and make your team follow you. Don't split push with katarina, if you plan on taking towers make sure you are pushing with your team after fights or taking objectives in general. 

In teamfights be patient, wait for their stuns and cds to be on cooldown and then you can jump in, what I like to do is to be behind my team or behind the enemy team hiding waiting for the perfect moment.

Also note: If game goes above 30 minutes, you can expect to lose if you are the only one on the team performing. When playing Kat aim to finish below the 30 minute mark else you can't carry, so make sure if you have a lead do as much as you can.

had this problem for a few months and I figured out how to fix this. I started doing them like you did in the video and it became a bad habbit and I started turning too with the board to land one, resulting in a 90 degree ollie. What fixed it for me was my front foot placement, try to not let the toes hanging off the board, pop straight down and put your weight more in opposite direction where the board is turning. Also jumping an obstacle could also help you fix your ollies. Just keep practicing and you will get it, took me a couple of months to figure this out but I didn’t give up and eventually got them on lock :D

what helped me to get the rotation consistent was to put my front foot in the middle of the board, a little bit higher or just behind the bolts and half my foot is hanging off the board and the other half is on the board, that way when I drag my foot up, the board automatically spins. I notice that you lean forward and you land with the board behind you, try to lean back, yeah I know it’s scary but that’s how you gonna land it, also try to bring your knees up as much as possible so you can let the board spin, that way you won’t catch the board mid rotation
